CONFIDENCE: 0.63  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the characteristic anhydride C=O doublet: very strong bands at 1795 cm⁻¹ (ν-sym) and 1875 cm⁻¹ (ν-asym), with weaker companion peaks at 1816–1842 cm⁻¹ and 1905 cm⁻¹, matching the known 1760–1790 / 1810–1860 cm⁻¹ pattern of cyclic anhydrides. A prominent band at 649 cm⁻¹ coincides with ν(C–Cl) stretches (rule GFQ-046), indicating chlorinated functionality. Additional medium bands near 1213 and 1256 cm⁻¹ are typical of anhydride C–O–C stretches, and the 552 cm⁻¹ shoulder fits another C–Cl deformation. Among the candidates, only molecule 1 (O=C1OC(=O)C(Cl)=C1Cl), a dichlorinated maleic anhydride, contains both a cyclic anhydride moiety and C–Cl bonds, fully explaining the observed double carbonyl pattern plus the halogen-specific low-frequency peaks.
